new_hypothesis.name: boost_velocity_burst
new_hypothesis.mechanism: DexScreener's free /token-boosts/latest/v1 endpoint (60 req/min, no auth) reports cumulative `totalAmount` of paid boosts per Solana token. A boost is purchased real-money attention (~$10/boost in packs). The long-term return on boost-existence is negative (-48% per Dethective), which is why no one trades on raw boost presence. But the EDGE is in the *velocity*: when a token's boost-count jumps by >=30 inside a 5-minute window, the project paid $300+ for a coordinated burst — economically rational only if there's a parallel marketing push (KOL drop, community pump, Twitter campaign) imminent or already firing. Retail clicks the boosted listing -> retail buys -> mechanical 5-15 min momentum window. The bot would NOT enter on boost-existence, but on velocity-acceleration + liquidity-floor + age-window + price-not-already-extended. Importantly: bot already polls these boosts to sol_dex_boosts_log.json (383 KB on disk) — the velocity signal is sitting unused.
new_hypothesis.persistence: Three layers. (a) Quant bots IGNORE boosts because long-term return is negative (-48%); they lose money holding to zero. We don't hold to zero — we exit at +12% TP / -7% SL / 12-min hard time stop, capturing only the retail-click micro-window. (b) Retail-click latency from boost activation to volume bump is empirically ~5-15 min (anyone clicking a boosted listing isn't a millisecond-bot — they're a human clicking through DexScreener trending). MEV/sandwich bots are present but they don't compete for directional momentum, only intra-block extraction. (c) The signal degrades only if boost-velocity becomes commoditized — but this requires the broader memecoin-bot population to specifically watch boost-deltas (not absolute counts), which is a different mental model from what's written about. Estimated half-life: 60-120 days before commoditization risk; rotate sizing down at that point.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: (1) Poll DexScreener /token-boosts/latest/v1 every 30-60s, append to existing sol_dex_boosts_log.json schema with a per-mint timestamp. (2) Compute rolling 5-min delta: boost_delta_5m = boost_now - boost_5min_ago for each Solana mint. (3) Trigger fires when ALL: boost_delta_5m >= 30 AND token_age_minutes between 30 and 720 AND liquidity_usd >= $15k AND vol_5m >= $5k AND price_5m_change between -10% and +25% (avoid extended chases) AND RugCheck score >= 50 AND GoPlus passes AND mint not already in cooldown AND mint not in our prior-boost-no-pump blacklist (anti-repeat). (4) Size: 0.15x tiny per OPERATOR_AUTONOMY_GRANT untested-strategy lifecycle. (5) Position management: 12-min hard time stop (vs default 60min — boost momentum is short), 12% TP target, 7% stop loss, 4% trailing arms at +6% gain. (6) Persistence: log every fire to sol_boost_velocity_log.json with pre/post outcome for backtest validation. (7) Run as additional strategy alongside copy_trade / fresh_profile / GBB — orthogonal funnel.
new_hypothesis.data_required: ZERO new HTTP API. Already-polled DexScreener /token-boosts/latest/v1 (free, 60/min, no auth) and /token-boosts/top/v1. Already-existing sol_dex_boosts_log.json on disk. New module ~150 LOC: boost_velocity.py tails the log, computes 5-min rolling delta per mint, emits signal events; new strategy entry boost_velocity_burst in degen_bot.py _evaluate_strategies; reuses existing security gate (RugCheck/GoPlus), Jupiter execution, position manager. proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: REQ-013 explicitly asked for the discriminator/log-line/CPI signature, >=2 recent grad tx signatures for smoke test, ALCHEMY logsSubscribe support confirmation, and rate-limit constraints. Subagent-1 + Subagent-2 cross-validated. RESULT: (a) GRADUATION SIGNATURE — Anchor instruction discriminator on LanMV9sAd7wArD4vJFi2qDdfnVhFxYSUg6eADduJ3uj. migrate_to_amm = cf52c091fecf91df, migrate_to_cpswap = 885cc8671cda908c. Computed via sha256('global:NAME')[0:8], cross-verified against live LaunchLab buy_exact_in (faea0d7bd59c13ec), sell_exact_in (9527de9bd37c981a), initialize_v2 (4399af27da102620) seen on-chain in subagent-1's 5-tx live decode AND independently re-computed by the orchestrator with python's hashlib — both match. NOTE: subagent-2's value 0x9beae792e0c6f17d is INCORRECT, do not use. (b) letsBONK QUALIFIER — the instruction's accounts array MUST include FfYek5vEz23cMkWsdJwG2oa6EphsvXSHrGpdALN4g6W1 (platform_config). Without that, the migration is from a non-letsBONK launch on the same LaunchLab program. Per Bitquery docs, this is exactly the production filter. (c) BELT-AND-SUSPENDERS — migrate_to_amm CPIs to AMM v4 675kPX9MHTjS2zt1qfr1NYHuzeLXfQM9H24wFSUt1Mp8 (initialize2, discriminator 0x01); migrate_to_cpswap CPIs to CPMM CPMMoo8L3F4NbTegBCKVNunggL7H1ZpdTHKxQB5qKP1C (initialize). Validating the inner-CPI is present rules out the false-positive aggregator-route case (subagent-2 found tx 3u7NMfKTbLL1k77S6aQJNQAP1qKRCwXA4FKoFXRqznrjw9wkLvEViUTqQDdDxeKYSYApH2u7Sgoiuh7hcy1ZT1R6 routes through both LaunchLab and CPMM as a user swap, not a graduation — the disambiguator is: graduation has the LaunchLab instruction at TOP LEVEL with platform_config in accounts, while routes have LaunchLab as a CPI-callee from an aggregator program). (d) RECENT TX SIGNATURES — neither subagent retrieved verified recent grad signatures: subagent-1 was budget-blocked, subagent-2 scanned 1000+ LaunchLab txs in ~10 min of mainnet activity and saw 0 graduations (graduations are <0.1% of LaunchLab traffic). RECOMMENDED PROCUREMENT PATH for ship-time smoke test: run a Bitquery IDE query (free tier) at https://ide.bitquery.io filtered Program=LanMV9..., Method IN [migrate_to_amm,migrate_to_cpswap], Accounts includes FfYek5..., orderBy desc Block.Time, limit 5 — returns recent grad tx hashes for a 5-tx end-to-end test. (e) ALCHEMY logsSubscribe — supports {mentions:[LanMV9...]} server-side filter syntactically (subagent-2 subscribed successfully; subscription ID returned), BUT delivers FAR FEWER messages than tx-rate (<0.1 msg/s observed vs ~1.7 tx/s actual) because LaunchLab is overwhelmingly a CPI-callee, not a top-level program — Alchemy's mentions filter elides CPI-only mentions. THIS IS A SHIP-BLOCKER for the WS path. RECOMMENDED IMPLEMENTATION: HTTP polling — getSignaturesForAddress(LanMV9..., limit=100) every 30s, dedupe against last-seen-sig, getTransaction(json,base58) on each new sig, decode top-level instructions, match on programId+discriminator+platform_config-account. ~1.7 tx/s × 30s = ~50 sigs per poll, at ~2 KB each via getTransaction = manageable. NOT WebSocket. (f) ALCHEMY LIMITS — connections 100 free/2000 paid; subscriptions 1000/conn; in-flight 200/conn; CU/s rolling 10s window with 429-on-overage; pings server-driven, client must auto-pong; reconnect-on-close mandatory.

The 1-6h-bucket -0.488 SOL drag is 84% concentrated in COPY_TRADE (-0.4075 SOL across 181 trades). Of THAT, 20 trades = -0.4274 SOL are -100% reconcile/orphan rugs. Moderate losers in the 1-6h copy_trade cohort sum to only -0.0493 SOL. A 'widen stop to 12% after 60 min' rule would NOT have caught any of the rugs (they go from positive/neutral straight to -100% at the rug-pull moment, not via slow drift past 8%) AND would HARM 7 strategies that are NET POSITIVE in the 1-6h bucket: fresh_profile (+0.0045 N=3 WR 100%), consensus_boost (+0.0044 N=5 WR 80%), bear_strength (+0.0031 N=3 WR 67%), bounce_hunter (+0.0045 N=4 WR 50%), profile_survivor (+0.0017 N=9 WR 33%), veteran_momentum (+0.0031 N=4 WR 75%), quiet_accum (+0.0112 N=14 WR 43%). Total positive 1-6h SOL across these 7 = +0.033 SOL. The CORRECT fix is COPY_TRADE-ONLY rug-detection via mid-hold liquidity-drop monitoring.
proposals_for_survival_brain.baseline: Per sol_strategy_stats.json: copy_trade all-time N=537 WR 33.7% pnl_sol -0.830 SOL avg_loss% -20.32% stop_loss_rate% 46.2% RR 0.72 PF 0.35. 1-6h cohort within copy_trade: N=181 WR 43.1% mean_pnl% -9.85% stop_rate 2.8% sum_sol -0.4075 SOL. Of those 181: 20 are -100% reconcile/orphan rugs summing -0.4274 SOL; 161 are non-rug trades summing -0.0493 SOL net (essentially break-even).
proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: If a copy_trade-only mid-hold liquidity-drop guardrail catches HALF the rugs at -50% before they go to -100%, savings ≈ 10 trades × 0.0214 SOL avg position size × 0.5 = +0.107 SOL retained. Realistic conservative estimate: catches 40% of rugs at -60% avg (vs -100%) = +0.085 SOL retained. Still a 17% reduction in 1-6h drag, dwarfing the original Option-B prediction's +0.32 SOL claim that turns out to have been mis-attributed (slow bleeders aren't the problem).
proposals_for_survival_brain.kill_criteria: Post-deploy rolling N=30 copy_trade trades held >60min: if liquidity-trigger fires <5% of the time the cohort = it doesn't see rugs (raise sensitivity from 40% drop to 30% drop). If salvaged loss <0.05 SOL after N=30 = the trigger is too late (tighten to 30-second polling instead of 60-second). If false-positive rate (trigger fires AND pool was actually healthy AND price recovered) >20% of triggers, threshold too sensitive — relax to 60% drop. If after N=50 trades the salvage is <0.03 SOL net (less than 6% of expected), revert and explore alternative rug-detection (deployer-wallet sell pattern, top-holder concentration spike).
proposals_for_survival_brain.min_sample_size: N=30 copy_trade trades held >60min for first kill check (~3-4 weeks at current copy_trade dormancy; faster if copy_trade fires accelerate). N=50 for full evaluation.
proposals_for_survival_brain.regime_scope: ANY (rug-pulls happen in all regimes; this is mechanical exit-management, not a directional edge).
proposals_for_survival_brain.rollback_plan: Single config flag: copy_trade_liquidity_guardrail_enabled=False, OR remove the periodic liquidity-poll loop from copy_trade position management. ~30 LOC revert. Original 8% stop and 60-min time-limit unchanged.
proposals_for_survival_brain.risk_if_wrong: Worst case: false-positive triggers exit healthy positions early at -30% to -50% (vs the +43% WR floor showing some trades recover from drawdown to TP). At 20% false-positive rate × N=30 trades × 0.0214 SOL avg × 8% premature exit = -0.013 SOL drag worst case. Bounded and small.
proposals_for_survival_brain.implementation_hint: (1) When a copy_trade position has been open >60 min, start polling that pool's liquidity_usd every 60s via DexScreener (existing infrastructure). (2) Compute rolling baseline = max(liquidity at entry, max(liquidity over first 60min)). (3) Trigger force-exit if liquidity_usd_now / liquidity_baseline < 0.6 (40% drop). (4) Log all triggers to sol_copytrade_rug_guard_log.json with: pool, entry_liq, baseline_liq, trigger_liq, drop_pct, exit_pnl_pct. (5) DO NOT apply this to other strategies — fresh_profile / consensus_boost / etc. are net-positive in 1-6h and don't need rug detection (they have other filter signals catching deployer risk pre-entry). (6) IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO RESEARCH-142: the proposed 'widen stop 8%->12% after 60min' rule should NOT ship — see baseline above for why.
